business_problem: GLS needed to replace a high-maintenance on-prem analytics platform that could explain past delays but could not predict future delivery problems, and whose slow queries, outages, and operational overhead limited the company’s ability to provide dependable forecasts to customers.
solution_summary: GLS rebuilt its analytics estate on Snowflake's AI Data Cloud running on AWS and paired the migration with a data-mesh operating model. Snowflake now serves as the company's cloud-only database and central analytics store, giving satellite teams governed access to data instead of routing every report through one central team. Because Snowflake scales on demand and requires near-zero maintenance, large queries no longer disrupt operations and the platform supports predictive-delivery use cases alongside routine reporting. GLS also added AI-assisted natural-language access that converts written questions into SQL and visualizations, helping business users get answers without learning complex interfaces. The combination of cloud scalability, shared data ownership, and low-friction analytics delivery cut reporting times dramatically, lowered total operating costs, and improved the reliability of delivery forecasts across a parcel network that spans 220 countries and territories.

solution_components.name: Snowflake AI Data Cloud

solution_components.name: Amazon Web Services (AWS)

data_flow: Parcel and operational data is centralized in Snowflake on AWS, shared to domain teams through a data-mesh model, queried directly or through natural-language AI assistance, and turned into last-mile and closing reports that support delivery forecasting and customer updates.
business_outcome: GLS reduced report-generation time by 92%, lowered total operating expenditure by 50%, improved some query performance by up to 10x, cut last-mile report preparation from 12 hours to 1 hour, and gave customers more reliable delivery forecasts through faster, more transparent analytics.
